bib.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

question: What makes masked autoencoding different between vision and language, and can a simple MAE scale self-supervised pre-training of vision transformers?
hypothesis: Because images are spatially redundant, masking a very high portion of random patches with an asymmetric encoder-decoder gives a nontrivial, scalable pretext task.
contributions: Asymmetric encoder-decoder: encoder sees only visible patches, lightweight decoder reconstructs with mask tokens
Very high masking ratio (75%) gives a meaningful task and 3x or more faster training
Vanilla ViT-H reaches 87.8% on ImageNet-1K-only; transfer beats supervised pre-training on detection, segmentation, classification

method.summary: Divide image into 16x16 (14x14 for ViT-H) non-overlapping patches, randomly mask 75%, encode visible patches only with a ViT, then a small Transformer decoder with shared learned mask tokens reconstructs pixels of masked patches with MSE loss. Pre-train on ImageNet-1K, evaluate by end-to-end fine-tuning, linear probing, partial fine-tuning and transfer.
method.task: self-supervised image pre-training (masked image modelling) and downstream recognition

datasets.name: ImageNet-1K
datasets.split: train set for pre-training (no labels); validation set for top-1 of single 224x224 crop
datasets.preprocessing: RandomResizedCrop (with horizontal flip); no color jitter

other.default decoder: 8 blocks, 512-d, 9% FLOPs per token vs ViT-L

models.name: MoCo v3, DINO, BEiT, supervised ViT

other.BEiT: tokenizer dVAE pre-trained on 250M DALLE images

training.objective: MSE between reconstructed and original pixels, on masked patches only (normalized per-patch pixels in main results)
training.lr: base lr 1.5e-4, lr = base lr x batchsize / 256
training.seq_len: 196 patches at 224; 25% (49) visible to encoder at 75% masking
training.regularisation: no color jitter, drop path, or gradient clip
training.wall_clock: ViT-L 1600 epochs: 31 hours on 128 TPU-v3 cores

other.fine-tune: AdamW lr 1e-3, wd 0.05, betas 0.9,0.999, layer-wise lr decay 0.75, batch 1024, cosine, warmup 5, epochs 100 (B) / 50 (L/H), RandAug(9,0.5), label smoothing 0.1, mixup 0.8, cutmix 1.0, drop path 0.1 (B/L) 0.2 (H)
other.linear probe: LARS lr 0.1, wd 0, momentum 0.9, batch 16384, cosine, warmup 10, 90 epochs, RandomResizedCrop, extra BatchNorm (affine=False) before classifier
other.partial fine-tune: Table 9 setting with epochs searched in {50,100,200}
other.supervised scratch recipe: AdamW lr 1e-4, wd 0.3, betas 0.9,0.95, batch 4096, warmup 20, 300 (B) / 200 (L/H) epochs, EMA 0.9999, drop path 0.1 (B) 0.2 (L/H)
other.COCO: Mask R-CNN + FPN; lr, wd, drop path, epochs searched per entry
other.ADE20K: UperNet, 100 epochs, batch 16, lr searched, relative position bias on only in transfer
other.class token: auxiliary dummy token appended to encoder input

inference.samples: single run per entry; no seeds or error bars stated

eval.protocol: fine-tuning, linear probing, partial fine-tuning; hyperparameters searched per baseline on COCO/ADE20K; no seeds or significance tests, though Table 7 differences called statistically insignificant

availability.code: stated: will release COCO configs; no URL in text

results.claim: MAE ViT-H at 448 fine-tuning reaches 87.8% on ImageNet-1K, best among IN1K-only methods (prior best 87.1%).
results.setup: ViT-H/14, 1600 epoch normalized-pixel MAE, fine-tune at 448

results.claim: A 75% masking ratio is best for both fine-tuning and linear probing; linear probe 54.6 at 10% vs 73.5 at 75%.
results.quote: ratio of 75% is good for both linear probing and

results.claim: Skipping mask tokens in the encoder gives 2.8x wall-clock speedup for ViT-L (3.3x fewer FLOPs).
results.quote: a 2.8× wall-clock speedup in our implementation

results.claim: Encoder with mask tokens loses 14% linear probing accuracy.
results.quote: accuracy drops by 14% in linear probing.

results.claim: MAE-pretrained ViT-L fine-tuned reaches 84.9 vs 82.5 for supervised from scratch (our recipe) and 76.5 original.
results.setup: ViT-L/16, 800 epoch MAE, 50 epoch fine-tune vs 200 epoch scratch
results.table: Table 1d, row pixel (w/o norm), column ft

results.claim: Fine-tuning one block lifts ViT-L from 73.5 (linear probe) to 81.0; MAE beats MoCo v3 at any partial fine-tuning depth but trails it in linear probing.
MAE beats supervised pre-training on COCO box AP with ViT-L.
Predicting dVAE tokens is statistically no better than normalized pixels as the target.
results.table: Table 7, row pixel (w/ norm), column IN1K ViT-L

results.claim: MAE ViT-L linear probe 75.8% vs MoCo v3 77.6%: still behind contrastive in linear probing.
results.quote: Our MAE with ViT-L has 75.8% linear probing

results.claim: MAE is far more robust on ImageNet-A than supervised ViT-H (68.2 vs 33.1).
results.setup: ViT-H fine-tuned on IN1K, no extra tuning

results.claim: Training time ViT-L 1600 epochs MAE is 31 hours vs MoCo v3 36 hours for 300 epochs.

limits: Pretext task reconstructs pixels, which are not semantic entities; authors hypothesize semantics emerge
Linear probing remains worse than contrastive methods (MAE 75.8 vs MoCo v3 77.6 ViT-L)
Reflects dataset biases and may generate inexistent content (broader impacts)
No seeds, error bars or significance tests stated; COCO configs not given in text
Result uses vanilla ViT; authors expect advanced networks to do better
Longer schedules: no saturation seen at 1600 epochs, so reported numbers may understate
